headline: Fine-tuned ProGen generates antimicrobial peptides with interpretable probing analyses
label: Adapting Pretrained Biomolecular Language Models
summary: AMP prediction benchmarks show leakage and inconsistent evaluation, motivating standardized evaluation and curated noncanonical peptide data.
synthesis: The common thread is antimicrobial peptide work in which models are conditioned on curated task data rather than used as generic embeddings. XAMPGen fine-tunes ProGen on known antimicrobial peptides to generate candidates, then applies probing classifiers and self-attention analysis to interpret its layers. DBNAMP supplies a chemically curated resource of 1,859 antimicrobial peptide entries with noncanonical residues, modifications, and 3D conformers. A review of AMP databases and ML/DL prediction tools identifies leakage and inconsistent evaluation and proposes a reference evaluation framework. Peptorama addresses non-ribosomal peptide structure creation and comparison with BGC-predicted peptides, a related but separate problem. The new element is pairing adaptation of generative models with interpretability analysis, alongside standardized data and evaluation that constrain how such adaptation claims can be assessed.
